thread:
maria: Thinking out loud — we need to decide collector topology for traces. agent-side OTEL vs centralized gateway? tradeoffs on enrichment, batching, and retention. any strong opinions?
kevin: +1 to discussing. my quick take: agents are better for low-latency enriching (host attrs) and filtering before network egress. gateways are easier for global sampling and consistent exporter chaining. :thinking:
lina: Agent + gateway hybrid seems common. agent does light preprocessing and resource attr injection, gateway handles heavy processors (tail sampling, span-aggregation) to reduce storage.
ashley: Concern: if we push tail-based sampling to the gateway, we need to ensure the gateway receives all spans for a trace fast enough — otherwise sampling quality suffers. network resilience matters.
zack: Cost perspective: central gateways let us do expensive processors once; but they become a scaling bottleneck. we saw memory spikes with span_aggregation before. need hard limits and backpressure.
maria: Example flows: (A) agents send OTLP directly to storage (tempo/cortex) after filtering — simpler, but inconsistent sampling across regions; (B) agents -> regional gateway -> exporter chain -> long-term store. gateway gives a single place to add exporters (s3 for 90d archive).
kevin: For archival retention we should chain an S3 exporter after the OTLP/tempo exporter. exporter chaining example: otlp -> tempo + s3. tempo keeps 7d hot, s3 cold 90d. advantage: replay/archive later for rehydration.
lina: small config sketch: ```yaml
service:
  pipelines:
    traces/collector:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [memory_limiter, batch, attributes, tail_sampling]
      exporters: [tempo, s3]
    traces/agent-light:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes, batch]
      exporters: [gateway]
```
ashley: ordering matters — attributes processor should run before sampling if sampling rules depend on injected attrs (tenant_id, route). otherwise sample decisions are wrong. also anonymize PII before exporters if needed.
zack: We should also be explicit about per-tenant retention — gateway can apply routing_processor to send high-value tenants to longer retention exporters. low-value -> downsampled traces or only metrics.
maria: Ops question: how do we avoid gateway becoming a single point of failure? multi-AZ regional gateways with autoscale and queueing (kafka/sqs) between agent->gateway could help. but that adds infra complexity.
kevin: Another pattern: lightweight agents push to local tcp buffer on host, a small forwarder batches to gateway. That reduces load on gateway from many small connections.
lina: Regarding exporters: prefer OTLP/gRPC with compression for cost. but when chaining to S3 use a streaming exporter that writes ndjson blobs partitioned by date/tenant.
ashley: Sampling types: head-based at agent for quick cuts; tail-based at gateway for correctness where we need to keep error traces. implement tail with trace-id buffering window e.g., 1s-5s. tune according to p95 end-to-end latency.
zack: Memory limits: set memory_limiter with strict max_heap_mib and check OOMKill metrics. also monitor processor queue length. temp spikes during releases. infra-bot: deploy-gateway started for canary region us-west-2 :rocket:
maria: Ops playbook note: if gateway overloaded, fallback route agents directly to tempo with a more aggressive head-sample policy. need a config toggle.
kevin: UX for rollouts: expose a per-tenant retention config in the console (Redwood Console) so product teams can request 30/90/365d and see cost delta. this ties into billing.
lina: telemetry considerations: traces vs metrics vs logs — keep pipelines per-signal (separate processors/exporters) to avoid cross-signal bloat. but share common receivers.
ashley: Security/compliance: gateway must be able to apply KMS encryption for S3 archives and redact sensitive attrs. agent can't hold customer keys for Private deployments.
maria: action items: 1) prototype gateway chaining with tempo+s3 exporter in a canary region (zack+kevin) 2) draft attributes+sampling ordering doc (ashley+lina) 3) add fallback direct-exporter config for overloaded gateways (maria). sound good? :thumbsup:
zack: I'll start the canary infra template tonight and add memory_limiter defaults to the helm chart.
kevin: I'll pair with zack on exporter chunking and ndjson layout for S3.
ashley: I'll write the sampling/order doc and include config snippets + tests.
lina: I'll open a tiny RFC for per-tenant retention UX and how console toggles map to exporter rules.
maria: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the decision log. ping me if anything blocks.
